body:
I found this: 
- SHA: e6690d37204dbd7154d275df75d9d0f98f5d2526

Maybe the message could explain it.

@secondwtq Thanks for tracking down the commit. I was wondering if the `*_count` column being updated when `counter_cache` is not specified (or even set to false) in the `belongs_to` is the correct behavior or not.

So there's a couple of issues that I'd like to address independently. For the case where the counter cache is unspecified, I'd say the bug is that we are only updating in memory, but not in the database. In Rails 4.1, we are inconsistent about whether we update when unspecified or not. For example:

```
user = User.create!(comments: [Comment.new])
user.comments.destroy_all
```

That will set the counter cache to -1 both in memory and in the database. I think we need to address whether specifying the counter cache is required, or based on convention, and update the documentation accordingly.

As for the case with `counter_cache: true`, yeah that's definitely a bug which I'll dig into.

/cc @rafaelfranca On the issue of whether we should be updating counter caches when `counter_cache: true` is not specified. In 4.1 it seems there are more cases where we just do it when the column name exists, instead of requiring the cache to be required.

@sgrif That's because the hash

``` ruby
comments: [Comment.new, Comment.new]
```

is wrapped to

``` ruby
[[Comment.new, Comment.new]]
```

in the call stack (maybe at ActiveRecord::Associations::concat) and its length is 1.

If you try appending with <<, you'll get:

``` ruby
user = User.create!(comments: [Comment.new, Comment.new])

user.comments << Comment.new << Comment.new

user.comments_count: 3
user.comments_count: 4
```

So @negative it is not "fixed".

issue.title: Counter cache seems to broken in 4.2.1
issue.body:
When I create a new `Address` object I see the following error - `ActiveModel::MissingAttributeErrormissing attribute: address_count`

This was obviously working in 4.2.0

``` ruby
class Address < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :user, counter_cache: :address_count
end
```

issue.title: 4-2 backport: Move flattening records added to an association farther out
issue.body:
Backport 025187d9806ddfbdded15d0c7bd8341665ee40e9 for the `4-2-stable` branch.
### Summary

There are many ways that things end up getting passed to `concat`. Not all of those entry points called `flatten` on their input. It seems that just about every method that is meant to take a single record, or that
splats its input, is meant to also take an array. `concat` is the earliest point that is common to all of the methods which add records to the association. Partially fixes #18689
